speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have swelling in your right knee with a family history of similar issues. To narrow this down, please tell me if you have experienced any sudden "popping" sensation or rapid swelling shortly after injury? Also, is there a history of similar knee problems in your siblings or parents?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudogout is unlikely in an 18-month-old; the combination of spontaneous swelling, lack of trauma, and strong familial history (uncle) strongly suggests a hereditary crystal arthropathy, possibly CPPD or a rare metabolic disorder like Lesch-Nyhan syndrome variant, but given the age and "pop" history mentioned in my initial prompt which the patient denied (no injury), I suspect a structural anomaly like a congenital ACL deficiency or a bleeding diathesis like Hemophilia presenting with hemarthrosis. Let me clarify the bleeding history and check blood counts. REQUEST TEST: CBC, PT/INR, PTT. REQUEST TEST: Serum Uric Acid and Calcium.
